=== why the classification matters: each class has a different fix ===
  compulsory -> prefetch, larger blocks (more spatial locality captured)
  conflict   -> raise associativity, or pad / reorganise the data layout
             (note: a fully associative cache has NO conflict misses at all)
  capacity   -> only more capacity or a smaller working set helps
             (loop blocking / tiling is the classic software fix)

  the classification above is the standard approximation: a miss that disappears
  in a fully associative cache of the SAME size is attributed to conflict.
code:
BLOCK = 16
CACHE_BYTES = 1024
LINES = CACHE_BYTES // BLOCK

def trace():
    """三段特征明确的访问：冷启动、跨步冲突、超容量工作集"""
    t = []
    t += [0x0000, 0x0010, 0x0020]                  # 3 个新块 -> 强制缺失
    p2 = [0x0400, 0x0800, 0x0C00, 0x1000, 0x1400]  # 块号均为 64 的倍数 -> 都在 index 0
    t += p2 + p2                                   # 访问两轮：第二轮才是冲突缺失
    ws = [0x100000 + 0x10 * i for i in range(LINES + 8)]   # 72 块 > 64 行
    t += ws + ws                                   # 两轮：第二轮全部放不下 -> 容量缺失
    return t

def sim_direct(tr):
    tag = [None] * LINES
    res = []
    for a in tr:
        blk, idx = a // BLOCK, (a // BLOCK) % LINES
        tg = blk // LINES
        if tag[idx] == tg:
            res.append("hit")
        else:
            res.append("miss")
            tag[idx] = tg
    return res

def sim_fully_assoc(tr, cap_lines):
    """全相联 + LRU，容量相同：用作「冲突缺失」的参照"""
    frames, lru, clock = [], {}, 0
    res = []
    for a in tr:
        blk = a // BLOCK
        clock += 1
        if blk in frames:
            lru[blk] = clock
            res.append("hit")
        else:
            res.append("miss")
            if len(frames) < cap_lines:
                frames.append(blk)
            else:
                victim = min(frames, key=lambda f: lru[f])
                frames.remove(victim)
                del lru[victim]
                frames.append(blk)
            lru[blk] = clock
    return res

tr = trace()
d = sim_direct(tr)
fa = sim_fully_assoc(tr, LINES)

seen = set()
counts = {"compulsory": 0, "conflict": 0, "capacity": 0}
detail = []
for a, r, rfa in zip(tr, d, fa):
    blk = a // BLOCK
    if r == "hit":
        detail.append((a, "hit", "-"))
        continue
    if blk not in seen:
        counts["compulsory"] += 1
        detail.append((a, "miss", "compulsory (first touch)"))
    elif rfa == "miss":
        counts["capacity"] += 1
        detail.append((a, "miss", "capacity (would also miss fully associative)"))
    else:
        counts["conflict"] += 1
        detail.append((a, "miss", "conflict (would HIT fully associative)"))
    seen.add(blk)

print("=== 3C classification (direct-mapped %d B cache, %d B blocks, %d lines) ==="
      % (CACHE_BYTES, BLOCK, LINES))
print("  reference pattern:")
print("    phase 1: 3 fresh blocks                    -> compulsory misses")
print("    phase 2: 5 blocks all mapping to index 0, touched twice")
print("                                               -> conflict misses")
print("    phase 3: a 72-block working set, touched twice (> 64 lines)")
print("                                               -> capacity misses")
print()
print("  %8s %8s  %s" % ("address", "result", "classification"))
for a, r, c in detail:
    print("  0x%06X %8s  %s" % (a, r, c))

total = sum(counts.values())
print()
print("  %-14s %5s %7s" % ("class", "count", "share"))
for k in ("compulsory", "conflict", "capacity"):
    print("  %-14s %5d %6.1f%%" % (k, counts[k], 100.0 * counts[k] / total))
print("  %-14s %5d" % ("total misses", total))

print()
print("=== why the classification matters: each class has a different fix ===")
print("  compulsory -> prefetch, larger blocks (more spatial locality captured)")
print("  conflict   -> raise associativity, or pad / reorganise the data layout")
print("             (note: a fully associative cache has NO conflict misses at all)")
print("  capacity   -> only more capacity or a smaller working set helps")
print("             (loop blocking / tiling is the classic software fix)")
print()
print("  the classification above is the standard approximation: a miss that disappears")
print("  in a fully associative cache of the SAME size is attributed to conflict.")
